title: The Raceland, Bayou Boeuf and Des Allemands bands and their leaders
summary: Three nearby bands and their leaders (Mike Taylor, Paul Roja, Tooker, Johnny Hill); Miller took over the boys' band and discusses his birth year.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape
story.community_name: Opening the tape: name, birth date and birthplace

blocks.x: And how uh how many bands did they have out there around Raceland?
Two. Three. By the Zelmer had a band, Raceland had a band, and Bui, Louisiana had a band.
And what were the names of the bands?
Well they called it the Bui Band, By the Zelmer Band, and the Raceland Band. That's all they called it.
And who played in the band there?

Well now Mike Taylor had the band in the Bui. The name was Spencer Taylor but everybody called him Mike. And I can't think of all the fellas, they were the Sawmill guys, they called it Sawmill. Yeah. They didn't play until on Sundays you know. Couldn't play no other day. And that fella that came to teach me, Paul Rosi had a band in Baudis Elmo. And a fella named Tooker, I forget, Tooker, real name, but he had the band that raised it, the old men bands. And Johnny Hills, he was the boy that took over the young boy's band, but he never could play. He never could play. So they gave it to me see. But I didn't stay there. And I was after, when I got 16, 17, I went on endowment. When you were 17?

But I put it up though. It was going from 18 to 35. And I put it up. If you look it up, you find out I was born in 1894. But I was born, and I have to tell you the truth, but I was born in 1895 see. But after I put it up to 1894 I let it stay there see. But I was 17, I ain't no joke about that. And so out there how big would those bands be, the different ones? The band we had must have had about, I'll tell you. We had Johnny Hill, Claiborne Roy, Esau Lewis, David Lewis, Oscar Shields, Joseph Pugh, Sullivan Pugh, Joseph Phillip, and what they named, Dukes, Arthur Dukes, and myself, Daniel Hadley, that's 11, and Kemp Hadley, Holly Taylor. Oh man, they had about 18 pieces. Gee, that's a big band. Yeah.
